name: customer-support-agent
tagline: Where questions sail in, dive for answers, and sometimes ask for a human
summary: A Next.js customer support chat. The browser sends the chat to one API route, which searches an AWS Bedrock knowledge base, asks Claude to answer in strict JSON (answer, mood, categories, hand-off flag), and checks that JSON. The page shows the answer, and two optional sidebars show Claude's reasoning and the sources it used.

entities.name: Home page
entities.summary: The one page of the app. It shows the top bar, the chat in the middle, and the two side panels if they are turned on.
entities.details:
- Left and right sidebars load only in the browser (ssr: false)
- Each sidebar shows only if its env flag is exactly "true"
- Flags: NEXT_PUBLIC_INCLUDE_LEFT_SIDEBAR and NEXT_PUBLIC_INCLUDE_RIGHT_SIDEBAR

entities.name: Chat area
entities.summary: The chat box where the user types. It sends the whole chat history to the server and swaps in the answer when it comes back.
entities.details:
- Adds your message plus an empty 'Thinking...' placeholder right away
- POSTs messages, chosen model and chosen knowledge base id to /api/chat
- On success, replaces the placeholder with the answer JSON
- Fires window events 'updateSidebar' and 'updateRagSources' for the side panels
- Clicking a suggested question sends it as a new message

entities.name: Model and knowledge base picker
entities.summary: Two drop-downs in the chat header. They pick which Claude model answers and which knowledge base is searched.
entities.details:
- Default model is claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
- Three models are listed: Claude 3 Haiku, Claude 4.5 Haiku, Claude 3.5 Sonnet
- The knowledge base list is a placeholder ('your-knowledge-base-id') you must edit
- Both choices are sent with every request

entities.name: Chat API route
entities.summary: The server door at POST /api/chat. It runs the whole job: search the knowledge base, ask Claude, check the answer, send it back.
entities.details:
- Reads messages, model and knowledgeBaseId straight from the request body
- Uses only the latest message as the search query
- Sends RAG sources back in an 'x-rag-sources' header
- Sends a short debug blob in an 'X-Debug-Data' header
- Gives each answer a fresh random id

entities.name: Answer shape check
entities.summary: Makes sure Claude's reply is real JSON with the right fields. If anything breaks, the user gets a polite 'sorry' with status 500.
entities.details:
- First escapes raw newlines inside string values, then JSON.parse
- Then a Zod schema checks every field and the allowed mood words
- Any error (API, parse, schema) lands in one catch block
- The catch returns a fixed sorry message, status 500

source.anchor: "Sorry, there was an issue processing your request. Please try again later.",

guard.rule: Claude's answer must be valid JSON that matches the response schema
guard.checks: JSON.parse after newline fix, then responseSchema.parse (user_mood must be one of 6 words, debug.context_used required)
guard.onFail: Throws, and the route returns a fixed 'Sorry, there was an issue...' body with status 500

entities.name: Retrieval limits
entities.summary: Rules that keep the knowledge base search small and safe. No id means no search; at most 3 chunks are fetched; only 1 is shown as a source.
entities.details:
- Missing knowledgeBaseId: returns empty context and isRagWorking false
- Asks Bedrock for numberOfResults n = 3
- Drops chunks that have no text
- All kept chunks go into the prompt, but only the first is sent to the sidebar (.slice(0, 1))
- Any error is caught and turned into an empty result

guard.rule: Search only with a knowledge base id, and fetch at most 3 chunks
guard.checks: knowledgeBaseId is truthy; numberOfResults: n (default 3); chunks must have content.text
guard.onFail: Returns { context: '', isRagWorking: false, ragSources: [] } so Claude is told 'No information found'

entities.name: Knowledge search (RAG)
entities.summary: Looks up the user's latest message in the knowledge base and returns matching text. This text is pasted into Claude's instructions.
entities.details:
- Runs before Claude is called, every time (it is not a tool Claude chooses)
- Turns each result into a source: id, file name, snippet, score
- File name is cleaned: underscores become spaces, '.txt' removed
- Joins all chunk texts with blank lines into one context string

entities.name: AWS Bedrock knowledge base
entities.summary: Amazon's hosted vector search. It holds your support documents and returns the closest chunks for a query.
entities.details:
- Client is fixed to region us-east-1
- Uses BAWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and BAWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY env vars
- At startup it only logs whether those keys exist; it does not stop the app
- Called with a RetrieveCommand

entities.name: Support categories
entities.summary: A JSON list of 8 support categories, like billing or technical. Claude is asked to tag each question with matching ones.
entities.details:
- Ids: account, billing, feature, internal, legal, other, technical, usage
- Each has keywords, but only the ids are sent to Claude
- USE_CATEGORIES = true turns the tagging on
- The left sidebar shows an icon for each known id

entities.name: Support system prompt
entities.summary: The instructions Claude gets. It pastes in the knowledge base text, lists the categories, sets the redirect rules and the exact JSON shape to reply in.
entities.details:
- Says: only use the information given
- If RAG failed, it says 'No information found for this query.'
- Redirect to a human if no info, off-topic, or the user asks for a person
- Includes two full JSON examples (normal and redirect)
- Company is hard-coded as Anthropic; change it for your use

entities.name: Support assistant
entities.summary: Claude acting as the first-line support agent. It reads the chat, answers in JSON, guesses the user's mood and suggests follow-up questions.
entities.details:
- Gets the full chat history from the browser
- The route adds an assistant turn with just '{' so Claude starts straight in JSON
- max_tokens 1000, temperature 0.3
- The '{' is glued back on before parsing
- Has no tools; search is done for it beforehand

agent.role: First point of contact: answers from the knowledge base, tags categories, rates mood, decides when to hand off to a human
agent.model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (default; user can switch in the picker)

entities.name: Anthropic API
entities.summary: Claude's servers. The route calls messages.create once per user message.
entities.details:
- Key comes from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
- No check that the key exists before calling
- The model name is whatever the browser sent

entities.name: Hand-off to human rule
entities.summary: When Claude says a human is needed, the server logs it and the chat shows a 'Talk to a human' button.
entities.details:
- The decision is made by Claude (redirect_to_agent.should_redirect), following the prompt rules
- Server only logs 'AGENT REDIRECT TRIGGERED!'
- Browser fires 'agentRedirectRequested' and shows the button
- Clicking fires 'humanAgentRequested' with mood hard-set to 'frustrated'

guard.rule: Hand the user to a human when Claude cannot or should not answer
guard.onFail: Shows a 'Talk to a human' button and fires browser events (no code listens to them)

entities.name: Message bubble
entities.summary: Draws one chat bubble. For the assistant it parses the stored JSON, shows a spinner while empty, then the answer as markdown.
entities.details:
- Empty response means 'Thinking...' spinner
- A 30 second timer flips to 'Something went wrong' if nothing arrives
- Renders markdown with raw HTML allowed (rehypeRaw) and code highlighting
- Shows suggested question chips under each assistant bubble

entities.name: Thinking sidebar
entities.summary: Left panel that shows Claude's private reasoning, the user's mood, whether context was used, and the matched categories.
entities.details:
- Listens for the 'updateSidebar' event
- Skips entries with a repeated id
- Keeps the newest 15 entries
- Mood colors: green positive, red negative, orange frustrated, and so on

entities.name: Sources sidebar
entities.summary: Right panel that lists which knowledge base snippet was used for each question, with a match score and a 'view full' popup.
entities.details:
- Listens for the 'updateRagSources' event
- Only adds an entry if there are sources AND Claude said context_used = true
- Score color: green above 60%, yellow above 40%, red below
- Keeps the newest 15 queries

quests.title: The opening brace
quests.prompt: Right before calling Claude, what does the route add to the end of the message list?
options: A user message saying 'Reply in JSON'
Nothing, it sends the messages as they are
quests.explain: It pushes { role: 'assistant', content: '{' } so Claude continues straight into JSON, then glues '{' back on before parsing.

quests.title: An angry mood
quests.prompt: Claude replies with user_mood: "angry". What happens?
quests.explain: The Zod schema only allows positive, neutral, negative, curious, frustrated, confused. The parse throws and the catch returns 500.

quests.title: When the server fails
quests.prompt: The route returns status 500 with a friendly sorry message. What does the user see?
quests.explain: The browser throws on !response.ok and never reads the body. The empty placeholder spins until the 30s timer fires.

quests.title: Three in, one out
quests.prompt: With a good match, how many knowledge chunks reach Claude's prompt, and how many show in the sources sidebar?
quests.explain: Bedrock is asked for 3 results and all go into the context, but ragSources is cut with .slice(0, 1).

quests.title: Who calls for a human?
quests.prompt: Who decides that the user should be handed to a human agent?
options: A keyword check in the route for words like 'human'
Claude, by setting redirect_to_agent.should_redirect in its JSON
The sources sidebar, when the match score is below 40%
The mood: any 'frustrated' user is redirected
quests.explain: There is no code rule. The system prompt tells Claude when to redirect, and the code only reacts to its should_redirect field.

quests.title: Searching for nothing
quests.prompt: Bedrock finds 0 results for the query. How does the search end?
options: Empty context but marked as working
quests.explain: No error is thrown, so isRagWorking stays true and the prompt gets an empty string instead of 'No information found'.

quests.title: Category tags
quests.prompt: What part of the categories JSON is actually sent to Claude?
options: Only the category ids, joined by commas
Ids, names and keywords as JSON
Nothing; categories are matched in code
quests.explain: categoryListString maps each category to c.id and joins them. Keywords are never used.

quests.title: Follow a question
quests.prompt: Watch one question travel from the route through search, Claude and the shape check.

cracks.title: 'Talk to a human' leads nowhere
cracks.hint: After the button fires its event, who is listening?
cracks.finding: The button dispatches 'humanAgentRequested' and the chat dispatches 'agentRedirectRequested', but no code in the app listens to either. A user who needs a person gets a button that only logs to the console.
cracks.suggestion: Add a listener that opens a real hand-off (ticket, live chat, email form) and tell the user what happens next.
decoys: The button text is too small to read
The redirect reason is not shown in the left sidebar
should_redirect is checked twice, once on the server and once in the browser

cracks.title: Errors hide behind a 30 second spinner
cracks.hint: The server sends a polite sorry message on failure. Does the browser read it?
cracks.finding: On a 500 the browser throws before reading the body, so the placeholder is never replaced. The user stares at 'Thinking...' for 30 seconds before 'Something went wrong' appears.
cracks.suggestion: On !response.ok, read the JSON body and replace the placeholder right away with its response text.
decoys: The 30 second timer is cleared too early
The spinner uses the wrong color

source.anchor: throw new Error(`API request failed with status ${response.status}`);

cracks.title: Browser picks the model and knowledge base
cracks.hint: Where do 'model' and 'knowledgeBaseId' come from, and who checks them?
cracks.finding: The route takes model and knowledgeBaseId straight from the request body with no allowlist or input check. Anyone can call /api/chat with the most costly model or any knowledge base the AWS keys can reach. An empty messages array even crashes before the try block.
cracks.suggestion: Validate the body with Zod and only accept model and KB ids from a server-side allowlist.
decoys: The API key is read on every request

source.anchor: const { messages, model, knowledgeBaseId } = await req.json();

cracks.title: Empty search counts as success
cracks.hint: What does isRagWorking say when Bedrock found nothing?
cracks.finding: When Bedrock returns zero chunks, retrieveContext still returns isRagWorking: true with an empty context. The prompt then pastes an empty block instead of 'No information found', which makes it less clear to Claude that it has nothing to go on.
cracks.suggestion: Set isRagWorking to false (or say 'No information found') when no chunk has text.
decoys: The file name loses its '.txt' ending
